implementation_groups.label: New codepoint over an existing primitive
implementation_groups.what_must_change: A table entry. The cryptography is already linked in on both sides.
implementation_groups.evidence: RFC 5702 s8.1: 'The signature scheme RSASSA-PKCS1-v1_5 is chosen to match the one used for RSA/SHA-1 signatures. This should ease implementation.'

implementation_groups.label: Same cryptography, new signalling
implementation_groups.what_must_change: Nothing cryptographic. A number that means 'I do X'.
implementation_groups.evidence: RFC 5155 s2: algorithm 7 is RSASHA1 and signals NSEC3 support; the signing maths is unchanged from algorithm 5.

implementation_groups.label: New record type on existing infrastructure
implementation_groups.what_must_change: Provisioning and RR support, but no new cryptography.
implementation_groups.evidence: RFC 7344 s3-4 defines CDS/CDNSKEY reusing the DS and DNSKEY wire formats verbatim.

implementation_groups.label: New cryptographic primitive
implementation_groups.what_must_change: A new curve or hash implemented in the signer AND the validator before anything is publishable.
implementation_groups.evidence: RFC 6605 s6 and RFC 8080 s5 both require validator support before a zone can safely sign with the algorithm.

implementation_groups.label: Parameter choice within an existing mechanism
implementation_groups.what_must_change: Zone configuration only; one operator acting alone.
implementation_groups.evidence: RFC 9276 s3.1: 'an iteration count of 0' and 's3.2: an empty salt', both configuration values of a mechanism already deployed.

implementation_groups.label: Deprecation
implementation_groups.what_must_change: Removal, by parties who already deployed. The observable is what PERSISTS, so onset is meaningless and residue is the quantity of interest.
implementation_groups.evidence: RFC 9905 s3: 'SHA-1 MUST NOT be used when creating DS records'; RFC 9906 s3 retires ECC-GOST.

implementation_groups.label: New DS digest type
implementation_groups.what_must_change: A hash implementation, and only on the parent's DS generator plus the validator. No signer changes and no key material changes.
implementation_groups.evidence: RFC 4509 s2 defines the DS digest as a hash over the child's DNSKEY: the child publishes nothing new. The first GOST digests observed (2011-05) sit on algorithm 5 and 8 keys, not algorithm 12 -- a GOST hash of an RSA key -- which is only possible because digest and signing algorithm are independent.

note: Onset bands come from the implementation groups, not the conceptual categories: a category mixes changes of very different implementation cost, so its onset spread is wide and says little. The groups are the predictive cut; the categories are the communicable one.
